title: Quentin and the Terminal
premise: Zephyrine Sterling is the last active terraformer on Meridian-9, a colony officially decommissioned decades ago, tending a seed-vault garden intended for settlers who will never arrive. When the ship Halcyon returns from a deep-space relay run with its crew biologically reversed into children who remember their own futures, Zephyrine realizes the colony's death was not an accident but an erasure, and that her memory logs are the only surviving record. Pursued by a corporate retrieval team sent to bury the evidence, she must carry the children and her archives to the edge-of-dead-space relay before its signal window closes forever. She reaches it at terrible cost, transmitting the truth outward as she chooses to stay behind with the garden, becoming both memory and root for whatever grows next.
about_author: August Thackeray is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations in the Arctic before turning to fiction. Their work explores loneliness, ecological grief, and the quiet heroism of people who maintain things no one remembers to value.

chapters.title: The Garden of Unborn Seasons
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Establishes her solitary routine on Meridian-9: tending the seed vault, recording daily logs for colonists who never came, speaking to plants as if they were descendants. The emotional beat is tender melancholy; she has made peace with being forgotten, or believes she has.

chapters.title: A Light That Should Not Be
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A ship breaches atmosphere after eleven years of silence: the Halcyon, presumed lost. She finds the crew aged backward into children who speak fragments of memories from lives they haven't lived yet, including accurate descriptions of her own logs. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, intercut with a child's fragmentary recollection. The children recall the colony's official 'decommissioning' as something deliberate and violent, contradicting everything in the corporate record. One child, Ivo, insists he died here once already. Beat: vertigo of unreliable time.

chapters.title: The Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Digging through sealed archives, she uncovers the Erasure Protocol: Meridian-9's population was logged out of existence to cover a terraforming failure, and the Halcyon's relay experiments fractured causality, sending its crew back through their own lifetimes. Beat: righteous anger replacing grief.

chapters.title: Ships on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Corporate retrieval ships enter orbit, sent to sanitize the site and the children. She fakes her own death in the greenhouse and flees with seven children and the archive cores toward the dead-space relay, three weeks' journey across dying terrain. Beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Dust Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Crossing the ash plains, the children experience cascading future-memories as they approach places where the timeline frayed. Ivo guides them past a sinkhole he 'remembers' swallowing them. Beat: the hunted finding agency; belonging forged between outcasts.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They reach the relay to find it failing, its signal window shortened by the same temporal damage that broke the Halcyon. To transmit the full archive she must physically splice the array during a storm, using herself as conductor. Beat: sacrifice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Signal Against Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. As Zephyrine splices the array, the retrieval team closes in; the children hold the line using their impossible foreknowledge of the soldiers' moves. The transmission begins, broadcasting the colony's true history to every listening station in human space. Beat: desperate, triumphant climax.

chapters.title: The Cost of Being Seen
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The transmission succeeds but the relay burns out; rescue will come, eventually, for the children. Zephyrine, injured by the splice, chooses to remain rather than slow them down, asking Ivo to remember her forward instead of backward. Beat: sorrow transfigured into gift.

chapters.title: First Season After
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, years later. Rescued children, now aging normally again, return to Meridian-9 as the first settlers of the reborn colony, carrying Zephyrine's logs like scripture. In the revived greenhouse, something she planted has bloomed. Beat: belonging achieved; memory becomes inheritance.
